sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa della guerra tra Iran e Israele, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è sceso del 18.93% a 20.90, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 20, indicando un mercato ancora difensivo. L'oro è salito del 4.01% a $4843.90/oz, mentre il Bitcoin è sceso dello 0.43% a $71,629. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi invariati al 2.00% (DFR) e 2.15% (Refi).
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the Iran-Israel war, negatively impacting equity markets and increasing demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX decreased by 18.93% to 20.90, but remains above 20, indicating a still defensive market. Gold rose by 4.01% to $4843.90/oz, while Bitcoin fell by 0.43% to $71,629. The ECB kept rates unchanged at 2.00% (DFR) and 2.15% (Refi).

market_impact_summary.it: La guerra tra Iran e Israele ha causato un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari, con il Nikkei che è salito del 5.39% e lo STOXX 600 del 3.62%. L'EUR/USD è salito dell'1.38% a 1.17, mentre il DXY è sceso del 0.90% a 98.74. Il petrolio è sceso del 13.45% a $94.57, riducendo la pressione inflazionistica. I tassi dei bond sono saliti, con il US 10Y Yield che è salito dello 0.18% a 4.34%.
market_impact_summary.en: The Iran-Israel war has had a negative impact on equity markets, with Nikkei up 5.39% and STOXX 600 up 3.62%. EUR/USD rose by 1.38% to 1.17, while DXY fell by 0.90% to 98.74. Oil prices plummeted by 13.45% to $94.57, easing inflationary pressures. Bond yields rose, with the US 10Y Yield up by 0.18% to 4.34%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con un tono positivo. Il Nikkei ha guadagnato il 5,39% a 56.308 punti, mentre lo Shanghai Composite ha salito del 2,69% a 3.995 punti. Anche l'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha registrato un aumento del 2,90% a 25.845 punti. Questi dati potrebbero anticipare un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un aumento dello 0,08% a 6.616,85 punti. Il Dollar Index (DXY) ha perso lo 0,90% a 98,74 punti. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, è sceso del 18,93% a 20,90 punti. I tassi di interesse sono stati poco mossi, con il tasso decennale USA che è salito dello 0,18% a 4,34%. L'oro ha guadagnato il 4,01% a 4.843,90 dollari l'oncia. Il mercato continua a mostrare un sentiment risk-off.

La situazione geopolitica rimane tesa. L'attenzione è focalizzata sulle possibili conseguenze dell'attacco iraniano. L'India ha deciso di mantenere invariato il tasso di interesse di riferimento in attesa di sviluppi nella crisi tra USA e Iran. Le unioni sindacali nel Regno Unito si preparano a una possibile battaglia per gli aumenti salariali nel settore pubblico a causa dell'inflazione.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, l'attenzione si concentra sui prossimi dati sul PIL degli Usa, in programma per il 29 aprile. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati nella riunione di pochi giorni fa. Il mercato continua a monitorare i dati economici per capire le prossime mosse delle banche centrali.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo il nostro deep dive con Bitcoin. La scorsa settimana, gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un deflusso netto di 159,1 milioni di dollari. Tecnicamente, il prezzo di Bitcoin si è mantenuto sopra i 71.000 dollari, con un incremento del 4,38% nella giornata di ieri, chiudendo a 71.710 dollari.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum ha mostrato una performance positiva, con un aumento del 7,09% e un prezzo di 2.256 dollari. Solana e Binance Coin hanno anch'esse registrato aumenti, rispettivamente del 5,74% e del 2,27%, con prezzi di 84,50 dollari e 613,33 dollari.

Per quanto riguarda il sentiment, l'indice Fear & Greed è sceso a 17, livello di Extreme Fear. Questo indice misura la psicologia del mercato, e un valore basso come questo potrebbe indicare una maggiore avversione al rischio tra gli investitori. La correlazione con i dati macroeconomici, come il recente tasso Fed Funds e le decisioni della BCE, resta da monitorare per capire come influenzeranno il mercato degli asset digitali nel breve termine.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is risk-off today, as indicated by the mixed performance in equities and a flight to safe-haven assets. The VIX index has dropped by 18.93%, while gold prices surged by 4.01%.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. The S&P 500 edged up by 0.08% on Friday. The STOXX 600 jumped 3.62%, and the Nikkei ended a strong session with a 5.39% gain. On the currency front, the EUR/USD pair rose to 1.17, up 1.38%. The dollar index (DXY) declined by 0.90% to 98.74. In commodities, gold prices soared to $4843.90 per ounce, while Brent crude plummeted by 13.45% to $94.57. US bond yields are slightly up, with the 10-year yield at 4.34%, and the 20-year TLT bond yield edged down by 0.01% to 86.64.

Key events to watch include the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, particularly between Iran and Israel. The Indian central bank has extended its pause on the key policy rate amid the US-Iran crisis. In the UK, pubs and restaurants are facing a 'permacrisis' after an energy shock, and unions are preparing for a public sector pay push as inflation bites. The European Central Bank's (BCE) recent rate decisions and upcoming CPI data from the Eurozone will also be closely monitored.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 

The recent BTC ETF daily net inflow has turned negative, coming in at $-159.1M. This shift may be contributing to the current price action in Bitcoin. 

In our BTC deep dive, we note that despite the negative ETF inflows, Bitcoin is still trading at $71,710, up 4.38% over the past 24 hours. This resilience could be a sign of strong underlying demand. However, it's worth noting that the price action has been influenced by broader market tensions, including the situation between Trump and Iran.

Moving on to altcoins, we see that Ethereum is up 7.09% to $2,256, while Solana is up 5.74% to $84.50. Binance Coin is up 2.27% to $613.33. These gains are a positive sign for the altcoin market, which has been relatively quiet in recent weeks.

In terms of sentiment and fear/greed, the Fear & Greed Index is currently at 17, indicating extreme fear. This could be a contrarian indicator, suggesting that we're near a local bottom. However, it's essential to keep in mind that market sentiment can shift rapidly, especially in the cryptocurrency space.

Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you tomorrow. A quick look ahead: keep an eye on market trends and we'll be back with more updates. Until then, goodnight and goodbye from Prais Alért. Have a great day.

articles.title: Iran’s Anti-Access and Area Denial Strategy Is Cruder Than China’s But Still Dangerous
articles.snippet: In past wars, commanders worried about what would happen after crossing the line of departure. Today, the concern is whether they can cross it at all. Surely this is a concern as the United States considers sending a Marine expeditionary unit into the Persian Gulf. Before they enter, whether by air or sea, the fight will already be underway. Meanwhile, closed shipping routes are increasing the costs of shipping, America’s Gulf partners are under continued pressure, and the Houthis fired a missile to underscore the point. The path to the battlefield is the battlefield. No longer a prelude.This is by The post Iran’s Anti-Access and Area Denial Strategy Is Cruder Than China’s But Still Dangerous appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Closing the Air and Missile Defense Gap in the Indo-Pacific
articles.snippet: During last summer’s 12-day war between Iran, Israel, and the United States, the U.S. military supported Israeli air and missile defense operations by utilizing its regionally deployed air and missile defense assets to intercept Iranian missiles and drones. By the time the shooting had stopped, CNN reported that the United States had expended 100 to 150 upper-tier, terminal-phase missile interceptors against Iranian missiles. This means that, in 12 days of fighting, the United States expended approximately 25 percent of its total stockpile — or 150 percent of annual global production at current production rates (though production increases are anticipated). The The post Closing the Air and Missile Defense Gap in the Indo-Pacific appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: The Campaign Ends at the Breach: Lessons from Ukraine on Why Armies Fail
articles.snippet: Somewhere behind the Novodarivka breach point in June 2023, Ukrainian armored formations sat staged and ready. The ammunition was there. The fuel was there. The original concept of operations called for 12 brigades to push through roughly 30 kilometers of frontage, isolate Tokmak within days, and drive south before Russian forces could consolidate. They never moved. The engineers could not open the lane. Without the lane, none of the rest of it mattered.Against prepared defenses, breaching and gap-crossing capacity can decide whether a land force ever gets to test the rest of its campaign design. articles.title: The Iran War’s Widening Impacts in the Middle East and North Africa
articles.snippet: The war with Iran has had ripple effects across the Middle East and North Africa. The Gulf Arab states, Iraq, and Jordan have suffered direct attacks from Iran, and Iraq also faces violence from Iranian-aligned militias. In response to an attack from Hizballah, Israel has intensively bombed parts of Lebanon and launched an expanded ground invasion in the south.While those countries coping with the direct impacts of the war receive — and deserve — attention, the war is also affecting other parts of the region, highlighting that the conflict will have wide-ranging and long-standing effects. We asked five experts to assess the impact so far The post The Iran War’s Widening Impacts in the Middle East and North Africa appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Jet Fuel Shortages May Persist for Months After Hormuz Reopens
articles.snippet: The restoration of normal jet fuel flows around the world will take months, even if Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz today, the head of the International Air Transport Association warned. “If it were to reopen and remain open, I think it will still take a period of months to get back to where supply needs to be given the disruption to the refining capacity in the Middle East, which is a critical part of the global supply of refined products, and not just jet fuel for other products as well,” Willie Walsh, director-general of IATA said,…
